[659](#659)
[660](#660)        wrapper_from_to_try_from!(impl[$($tv),*] TryFrom<$tf> for Vec1<$et> $($tail)*);
[661](#661)
[662](#662)        impl<$($tv)*> From<Vec1<$et>> for $tf $($tail)* {
[663](#663)            fn from(vec: Vec1<$et>) -> Self {
[664](#664)                vec.0.into()
[665](#665)            }
[666](#666)        }
[667](#667)    );
[668](#668)    (impl[$($tv:tt)*] TryFrom<$tf:ty> for Vec1<$et:ty> $($tail:tt)*) => (
[669](#669)        impl<$($tv)*> TryFrom<$tf> for Vec1<$et> $($tail)* {
[670](#670)            type Error = Size0Error;
[671](#671)
[672](#672)            fn try_from(inp: $tf) -> StdResult<Self, Self::Error> {
[673](#673)                if inp.is_empty() {
[674](#674)                    Err(Size0Error)
[675](#675)                } else {
[676](#676)                    Ok(Vec1(inp.into()))
[677](#677)                }
[678](#678)            }
[679](#679)        }

[1016](#1016)        proptest! {
[1017](#1017)            #[test]
[1018](#1018)            fn same_behavior_as_vec_except_when_empty(
[1019](#1019)                data in (1usize..=20)
[1020](#1020)                    .prop_flat_map(|size| prop::collection::vec(any::<bool>(), size..=size))
[1021](#1021)            ) {
[1022](#1022)                use std::convert::TryFrom;
[1023](#1023)
[1024](#1024)                let mut vec = data.clone();
[1025](#1025)                let mut vec1 = Vec1::try_from(data).unwrap();
[1026](#1026)                let last = *vec1.last();
[1027](#1027)
[1028](#1028)                vec.retain(|value| *value == true);
[1029](#1029)                let res = vec1.retain(|value| *value == true);
[1030](#1030)
[1031](#1031)                if vec.is_empty() {
[1032](#1032)                    assert_eq!(res, Err(Size0Error));
[1033](#1033)                    assert_eq!(vec1.len(), 1);
[1034](#1034)                    assert_eq!(vec1.last(), &last);
[1035](#1035)                } else {
[1036](#1036)                    assert_eq!(res, Ok(()));
[1037](#1037)                    assert_eq!(&*vec, &*vec1);
[1038](#1038)                }
[1039](#1039)
[1040](#1040)            }
[1041](#1041)        }

[1092](#1092)
[1093](#1093)        macro_rules! do_call_drain {
[1094](#1094)            ($vec:ident.drain($from:expr, $to:expr, $incl:expr) => $iter:ident => $map:block) => {{
[1095](#1095)                match ($from, $to) {
[1096](#1096)                    (Some(from), Some(to)) => {
[1097](#1097)                        if $incl {
[1098](#1098)                            let $iter = $vec.drain(from..=to);
[1099](#1099)                            $map
[1100](#1100)                        } else {
[1101](#1101)                            let $iter = $vec.drain(from..to);
[1102](#1102)                            $map
[1103](#1103)                        }
[1104](#1104)                    }
[1105](#1105)                    (None, Some(to)) => {
[1106](#1106)                        if $incl {
[1107](#1107)                            let $iter = $vec.drain(..=to);
[1108](#1108)                            $map
[1109](#1109)                        } else {
[1110](#1110)                            let $iter = $vec.drain(..to);
[1111](#1111)                            $map
[1112](#1112)                        }
[1113](#1113)                    }
[1114](#1114)                    (Some(from), None) => {
[1115](#1115)                        let $iter = $vec.drain(from..);
[1116](#1116)                        $map
[1117](#1117)                    }
[1118](#1118)                    (None, None) => {
[1119](#1119)                        let $iter = $vec.drain(..);
[1120](#1120)                        $map
[1121](#1121)                    }
[1122](#1122)                }
[1123](#1123)            }};
[1124](#1124)        }
[1125](#1125)
[1126](#1126)        proptest! {
[1127](#1127)
[1128](#1128)            #[test]
[1129](#1129)            fn works_as_in_vec_except_if_draining_all(
[1130](#1130)                data in prop::collection::vec(any::<u8>(), 1..=5),
[1131](#1131)                start in (0usize..7).prop_map(|v| if v == 7 { None } else { Some(v) }),
[1132](#1132)                end in (0usize..7).prop_map(|v| if v == 7 { None } else { Some(v) }),
[1133](#1133)                incl in any::<bool>()
[1134](#1134)            ) {
[1135](#1135)                use std::convert::TryFrom;
[1136](#1136)
[1137](#1137)                let mut data2 = data.clone();
[1138](#1138)                let res_vec = catch_unwind(move || {
[1139](#1139)                    let drained = do_call_drain!(data2.drain(start, end, incl) => iter => { iter.collect::<Vec<u8>>() });
[1140](#1140)                    (data2, drained)
[1141](#1141)                });
[1142](#1142)
[1143](#1143)                let mut data2 = Vec1::try_from(data.clone()).unwrap();
[1144](#1144)                let res_vec1 = catch_unwind(move ||{
[1145](#1145)                    let drained = do_call_drain!(data2.drain(start, end, incl) => iter_res => { iter_res.map(|iter| iter.collect::<Vec<u8>>()) });
[1146](#1146)                    (data2, drained)
[1147](#1147)                });
[1148](#1148)
[1149](#1149)                match (res_vec, res_vec1) {
[1150](#1150)                    (Err(_), Err(_)) => {},
[1151](#1151)                    (Ok(_), Err(panic)) => std::panic::resume_unwind(panic),
[1152](#1152)                    (Err(panic), Ok(_)) => std::panic::resume_unwind(panic),
[1153](#1153)                    (Ok((vec, vec_drained)), Ok((vec1, vec1_res))) => {
[1154](#1154)                        if vec.is_empty() {
[1155](#1155)                            assert_eq!(vec1_res, Err(Size0Error));
[1156](#1156)                            assert_eq!(&*vec1, &*data);
[1157](#1157)                        } else {
[1158](#1158)                            let vec1_drained = vec1_res.unwrap();
[1159](#1159)                            assert_eq!(vec_drained, vec1_drained);
[1160](#1160)                            assert_eq!(&*vec, &*vec1);
[1161](#1161)                        }
[1162](#1162)                    }
[1163](#1163)                }
[1164](#1164)            }
[1165](#1165)        }
[1166](#1166)

[1749](#1749)            #[test]
[1750](#1750)            fn hash() {
[1751](#1751)                let a = vec1![1u8, 10, 33, 12];

[1753](#1753)                a.hash(&mut hasher);
[1754](#1754)                let a_state = hasher.finish();
[1755](#1755)
[1756](#1756)                let b = a.into_vec();
[1757](#1757)                let mut hasher = DefaultHasher::new();
[1758](#1758)                b.hash(&mut hasher);
[1759](#1759)                let b_state = hasher.finish();
[1760](#1760)
[1761](#1761)                assert_eq!(a_state, b_state);
[1762](#1762)            }
[1763](#1763)

[1765](#1765)            fn hash_slice() {

[1768](#1768)                <Vec1<u8> as Hash>::hash_slice(a, &mut hasher);
[1769](#1769)                let a_state = hasher.finish();
[1770](#1770)
[1771](#1771)                let b: &[_] = &[std::vec![1u8, 10, 33, 12], std::vec![22, 12]];
[1772](#1772)                let mut hasher = DefaultHasher::new();
[1773](#1773)                <Vec<u8> as Hash>::hash_slice(b, &mut hasher);
[1774](#1774)                let b_state = hasher.finish();
[1775](#1775)
[1776](#1776)                assert_eq!(a_state, b_state);
[1777](#1777)            }

# vec1::smallvec_v1 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/vec1/1.12.1/vec1/smallvec_v1/index.html

**crate feature**only.

`smallvec-v1`## Expand description

A alternative `Vec1` implementation backed by an `SmallVec1`.

[§](https://docs.rs#construction-macro)Construction Macro

A macro similar to `vec!` or `vec1!` does exist and is
re-exported in this module as `smallvec1`.

Due to limitations in rust we can’t properly document it directly without either giving it strange names or ending up with name collisions once we support smallvec v2 in the future (without introducing a braking change).

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use vec1::smallvec_v1::{smallvec1, SmallVec1};
let v: SmallVec1<[u8; 4]> = smallvec1![1u8, 2];
assert_eq!(&*v, &*vec![1u8,2]);
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Small](https://docs.rs/struct.SmallVec1.html)- Vec1
- `smallvec::SmallVec`wrapper which guarantees to have at least 1 element.

---

# vec1 in vec1 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/vec1/1.12.1/vec1/macro.vec1.html

```
macro_rules! vec1 {
    () => { ... };
    ($first:expr $(, $item:expr)* , ) => { ... };
    ($first:expr $(, $item:expr)* ) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

A macro similar to `vec!` to create a `Vec1`.

If it is called with less then 1 element a
compiler error is triggered (using `compile_error`
to make sure you know what went wrong).

---

# Vec1 in vec1 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/vec1/1.12.1/vec1/struct.Vec1.html

`pub struct Vec1<I>(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

`std::vec::Vec` wrapper which guarantees to have at least 1 element.

`Vec1<T>` dereferences to `&[T]` and `&mut [T]` as functionality
exposed through this can not change the length.

Methods of `Vec` which can be called without reducing the length
(e.g. `capacity()`, `reserve()`) are exposed through wrappers
with the same function signature.

Methods of `Vec` which could reduce the length to 0
are return a `Result` wrapping their normal return type.

Methods with returned `Option<T>` with `None` if the length was 0
(and do not reduce the length) now return T. (e.g. `first`,
`last`, `first_mut`, etc.).

All stable traits and methods implemented on `Vec<T>` *should* also
be implemented on `Vec1<T>` (except if they make no sense to implement
due to the len 1 guarantee). Be aware implementations may lack behind a bit,
fell free to open a issue/make a PR, but please search closed and open
issues for duplicates first.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

This will fail if the input `Vec<T>` is empty.
The returned error is a `Size0Error` instance, as
such this means the *input vector will be dropped if
it’s empty*. But this is normally fine as it only
happens if the `Vec<T>` is empty.

If calls `drain` on the underlying vector if it will not empty the vector.

[§](https://docs.rs#error)Error

If calling `drain` would empty the vector an `Err(Size0Error)` is returned
**instead** of draining the vector.

[§](https://docs.rs#panic)Panic

Like [ Vec::drain()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html#method.drain) panics if:

- The starting point is greater than the end point.
- The end point is greater than the length of the vector.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/vec1/lib.rs.html#184-211)#### pub fn [retain](https://docs.rs#method.retain)<F>(&mut self, f: F) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [Size0Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Size0Error.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/vec1/lib.rs.html#184-211)

#### pub fn [retain](https://docs.rs#method.retain)<F>(&mut self, f: F) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [Size0Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Size0Error.html)>

Removes all elements except the ones which the predicate says need to be retained.

The moment the last element would be removed this will instead fail, not removing
the element. **All but the last element will have been removed anyway.**

[§](https://docs.rs#panic-behavior)Panic Behavior

The panic behavior is for now unspecified and might change without a major version release.

The current implementation does only delete non-retained elements at
the end of the `retain` function call. This might change in the future
matching `std`s behavior.

[§](https://docs.rs#error-1)Error

If the last element would be removed instead of removing it a `Size0Error` is
returned.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Is for `Vec1` but similar code works with `SmallVec1`, too.

```
let mut vec = vec1![1, 7, 8, 9, 10];
vec.retain(|v| *v % 2 == 1).unwrap();
assert_eq!(vec, vec1![1, 7, 9]);
let Size0Error = vec.retain(|_| false).unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(vec.len(), 1);
assert_eq!(vec.last(), &9);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/vec1/lib.rs.html#184-211)#### pub fn [retain_mut](https://docs.rs#method.retain_mut)<F>(&mut self, f: F) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [Size0Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Size0Error.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/vec1/lib.rs.html#184-211)

#### pub fn [retain_mut](https://docs.rs#method.retain_mut)<F>(&mut self, f: F) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [Size0Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Size0Error.html)>

Removes all elements except the ones which the predicate says need to be retained.

The moment the last element would be removed this will instead fail, not removing
the element. **All other non retained elements will still be removed.** This means
you have to be more careful compared to `Vec::retain_mut` about how you modify
non retained elements in the closure.

[§](https://docs.rs#panic-behavior-1)Panic Behavior

The panic behavior is for now unspecified and might change without a major version release.

The current implementation does only delete non-retained elements at
the end of the `retain` function call. This might change in the future
matching `std`s behavior.

[§](https://docs.rs#error-2)Error

If the last element would be removed instead of removing it a `Size0Error` is
returned.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

Is for `Vec1` but similar code works with `SmallVec1`, too.

```
let mut vec = vec1![1, 7, 8, 9, 10];
vec.retain_mut(|v| {
    *v += 2;
    *v % 2 == 1
}).unwrap();
assert_eq!(vec, vec1![3, 9, 11]);
let Size0Error = vec.retain_mut(|_| false).unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(vec.len(), 1);
assert_eq!(vec.last(), &11);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/vec1/lib.rs.html#184-211)#### pub fn [into_boxed_slice](https://docs.rs#method.into_boxed_slice)(self) -> [Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<[[I]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/vec1/lib.rs.html#184-211)

#### pub fn [into_boxed_slice](https://docs.rs#method.into_boxed_slice)(self) -> [Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<[[I]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html)>

Turns this vector into a boxed slice.

For `Vec1` this is as cheap as for `Vec` but for
`SmallVec1` this will cause an allocation if the
on-stack buffer was not yet spilled.

Leaks the allocation to return a mutable slice reference.

This is equivalent to turning this vector into a boxed slice and then leaking that slice.

In case of `SmallVec1` calling leak does entail an allocation
if the stack-buffer had not yet spilled.

Like [ Iterator::reduce()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html#method.reduce) but does not return an option.

This is roughly equivalent with `.into_iter().reduce(f).unwrap()`.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-2)Example

`assert_eq!(vec1![1,2,4,3].reduce(std::cmp::max), 4)`*Be aware that  reduce consumes the vector, to get a reference
use either reduce_ref or reduce_mut.*

Like [ Iterator::reduce()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html#method.reduce) but does not return an option.

This is roughly equivalent with `.iter().reduce(f).unwrap()`.

*Hint: Because of the reduction function returning a reference
this method is (in general) only suitable for selecting exactly
one element from the vector.*

Like [ Iterator::reduce()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html#method.reduce) but does not return an option.

This is roughly equivalent with `.iter_mut().reduce(f).unwrap()`.

*Hint: Because of the reduction function returning a reference
this method is (in general) only suitable for selecting exactly
one element from the vector.*

[§](https://docs.rs#example-4)Example

`assert_eq!(vec1![1,2,4,3].reduce_mut(std::cmp::max), &mut 4)`[Source](https://docs.rs/src/vec1/lib.rs.html#239-245)`?` use Vec1::try_from_vec() instead

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/vec1/lib.rs.html#239-245)

`?` use Vec1::try_from_vec() insteadTries to create a `Vec1<T>` from a `Vec<T>`.

The fact that the input is returned *as error* if it’s empty,
means that it doesn’t work well with the `?` operator. It naming
is also semantic sub-optimal as it’s not a “from” but “try from”
conversion. Which is why this method is now deprecated. Instead
use `try_from_vec` and once `TryFrom` is stable it will be possible
to use `try_from`, too.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-9)Errors

If the input is empty the input is returned *as error*.

Create a new `Vec1` by consuming `self` and mapping each element.

This is useful as it keeps the knowledge that the length is >= 1,
even through the old `Vec1` is consumed and turned into an iterator.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-5)Example

```
let data = vec1![1u8,2,3];
let data = data.mapped(|x|x*2);
assert_eq!(data, vec![2,4,6]);
// without mapped
let data = Vec1::try_from_vec(data.into_iter().map(|x|x*2).collect::<Vec<_>>()).unwrap();
assert_eq!(data, vec![4,8,12]);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/vec1/lib.rs.html#338-350)#### pub fn [try_mapped](https://docs.rs#method.try_mapped)<F, N, E>(self, map_fn: F) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Vec1](https://docs.rs/struct.Vec1.html)<N>, E>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/vec1/lib.rs.html#338-350)

#### pub fn [try_mapped](https://docs.rs#method.try_mapped)<F, N, E>(self, map_fn: F) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Vec1](https://docs.rs/struct.Vec1.html)<N>, E>

Create a new `Vec1` by consuming `self` and mapping each element
to a `Result`.

This is useful as it keeps the knowledge that the length is >= 1,
even through the old `Vec1` is consumed and turned into an iterator.

As this method consumes self, returning an error means that this
vec is dropped. I.e. this method behaves roughly like using a
chain of `into_iter()`, `map`, `collect::<Result<Vec<N>,E>>` and
then converting the `Vec` back to a `Vec1`.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-10)Errors

Once any call to `map_fn` returns a error that error is directly
returned by this method.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-6)Example

```
let data = vec1![1,2,3];
let data: Result<Vec1<u8>, &'static str> = data.try_mapped(|x| Err("failed"));
assert_eq!(data, Err("failed"));
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/vec1/lib.rs.html#363-373)

`split_off`, `try_split_off doesn't panic on out of bounds `at`

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/vec1/lib.rs.html#430-437)

#### pub fn [try_split_off](https://docs.rs#method.try_split_off)(&mut self, at: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Vec1](https://docs.rs/struct.Vec1.html)<T>, [Size0Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Size0Error.html)>

`split_off`, `try_split_off doesn't panic on out of bounds `at`Calls `split_off` on the inner vec if both resulting parts have length >= 1.

**In difference to  split_off this also returns a Size0Error if at is
greater then len. Which is different to how [Vec.split_off()] behaves.**

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-14)Errors

If after the split any part would be empty an error is returned as the length >= 1 constraint must be uphold.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/vec1/lib.rs.html#457-480)#### pub fn [splice](https://docs.rs#method.splice)<R, I>(
    &mut self,
    range: R,
    replace_with: I,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Splice](https://docs.rs/struct.Splice.html)<'_, <I as [IntoIterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.IntoIterator.html)>::[IntoIter](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.IntoIterator.html#associatedtype.IntoIter)>, [Size0Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Size0Error.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/vec1/lib.rs.html#457-480)

#### pub fn [splice](https://docs.rs#method.splice)<R, I>(
    &mut self,
    range: R,
    replace_with: I,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Splice](https://docs.rs/struct.Splice.html)<'_, <I as [IntoIterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.IntoIterator.html)>::[IntoIter](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.IntoIterator.html#associatedtype.IntoIter)>, [Size0Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Size0Error.html)>

Calls `splice` on the underlying vec (only) if it wont produce an empty vec.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-15)Errors

If range covers the whole vec and the replacement iterator doesn’t yield
any value an error is returned **instead of doing any splicing**.

**To check if the iterator will yield values we need to turn call next on it
once which means that if an error is returned **

`Iterator::next()` is still called once![§](https://docs.rs#panics-3)Panics

This **will** panic  under the same conditions as [ Vec::splice()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html#method.splice),
the conditions are:

- if the starting point is greater than the end point
- if the end point is greater than the length of the vector.

Returns a mutable reference to the first element of the slice, or `None` if it is empty.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-3)Examples

```
let x = &mut [0, 1, 2];
if let Some(first) = x.first_mut() {
    *first = 5;
}
assert_eq!(x, &[5, 1, 2]);
let y: &mut [i32] = &mut [];
assert_eq!(None, y.first_mut());
```

Returns a reference to an element or subslice depending on the type of index.

- If given a position, returns a reference to the element at that
position or `None`if out of bounds.
- If given a range, returns the subslice corresponding to that range,
or `None`if out of bounds.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-18)Examples

```
let v = [10, 40, 30];
assert_eq!(Some(&40), v.get(1));
assert_eq!(Some(&[10, 40][..]), v.get(0..2));
assert_eq!(None, v.get(3));
assert_eq!(None, v.get(0..4));
```
1.0.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#639-641)#### pub unsafe fn [get_unchecked](https://docs.rs#method.get_unchecked)<I>(
    &self,
    index: I,
) -> &<I as [SliceIndex](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/index/trait.SliceIndex.html)<[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html)>>::[Output](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/index/trait.SliceIndex.html#associatedtype.Output)

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#639-641)

#### pub unsafe fn [get_unchecked](https://docs.rs#method.get_unchecked)<I>(
    &self,
    index: I,
) -> &<I as [SliceIndex](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/index/trait.SliceIndex.html)<[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html)>>::[Output](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/index/trait.SliceIndex.html#associatedtype.Output)

Returns a reference to an element or subslice, without doing bounds checking.

For a safe alternative see [ get](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.get).

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

Calling this method with an out-of-bounds index is * undefined behavior*
even if the resulting reference is not used.

You can think of this like `.get(index).unwrap_unchecked()`.  It’s UB
to call `.get_unchecked(len)`, even if you immediately convert to a
pointer.  And it’s UB to call `.get_unchecked(..len + 1)`,
`.get_unchecked(..=len)`, or similar.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-20)Examples

```
let x = &[1, 2, 4];
unsafe {
    assert_eq!(x.get_unchecked(1), &2);
}
```
1.0.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#684-686)#### pub unsafe fn [get_unchecked_mut](https://docs.rs#method.get_unchecked_mut)<I>(
    &mut self,
    index: I,
) -> &mut <I as [SliceIndex](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/index/trait.SliceIndex.html)<[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html)>>::[Output](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/index/trait.SliceIndex.html#associatedtype.Output)

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#684-686)

#### pub unsafe fn [get_unchecked_mut](https://docs.rs#method.get_unchecked_mut)<I>(
    &mut self,
    index: I,
) -> &mut <I as [SliceIndex](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/index/trait.SliceIndex.html)<[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html)>>::[Output](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/index/trait.SliceIndex.html#associatedtype.Output)

Returns a mutable reference to an element or subslice, without doing bounds checking.

For a safe alternative see [ get_mut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.get_mut).

[§](https://docs.rs#safety-1)Safety

Calling this method with an out-of-bounds index is * undefined behavior*
even if the resulting reference is not used.

You can think of this like `.get_mut(index).unwrap_unchecked()`.  It’s
UB to call `.get_unchecked_mut(len)`, even if you immediately convert
to a pointer.  And it’s UB to call `.get_unchecked_mut(..len + 1)`,
`.get_unchecked_mut(..=len)`, or similar.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-21)Examples

```
let x = &mut [1, 2, 4];
unsafe {
    let elem = x.get_unchecked_mut(1);
    *elem = 13;
}
assert_eq!(x, &[1, 13, 4]);
```
Returns a raw pointer to the slice’s buffer.

The caller must ensure that the slice outlives the pointer this function returns, or else it will end up dangling.

The caller must also ensure that the memory the pointer (non-transitively) points to
is never written to (except inside an `UnsafeCell`) using this pointer or any pointer
derived from it. If you need to mutate the contents of the slice, use [ as_mut_ptr](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_mut_ptr).

Modifying the container referenced by this slice may cause its buffer to be reallocated, which would also make any pointers to it invalid.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-22)Examples

```
let x = &[1, 2, 4];
let x_ptr = x.as_ptr();
unsafe {
    for i in 0..x.len() {
        assert_eq!(x.get_unchecked(i), &*x_ptr.add(i));
    }
}
```
1.0.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#757)#### pub fn [as_mut_ptr](https://docs.rs#method.as_mut_ptr)(&mut self) -> [*mut T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html)

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#757)

#### pub fn [as_mut_ptr](https://docs.rs#method.as_mut_ptr)(&mut self) -> [*mut T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html)

Returns an unsafe mutable pointer to the slice’s buffer.

The caller must ensure that the slice outlives the pointer this function returns, or else it will end up dangling.

Modifying the container referenced by this slice may cause its buffer to be reallocated, which would also make any pointers to it invalid.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-23)Examples

```
let x = &mut [1, 2, 4];
let x_ptr = x.as_mut_ptr();
unsafe {
    for i in 0..x.len() {
        *x_ptr.add(i) += 2;
    }
}
assert_eq!(x, &[3, 4, 6]);
```
1.48.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#793)#### pub fn [as_ptr_range](https://docs.rs#method.as_ptr_range)(&self) -> [Range](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/range/struct.Range.html)<[*const T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html)>

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#793)

#### pub fn [as_ptr_range](https://docs.rs#method.as_ptr_range)(&self) -> [Range](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/range/struct.Range.html)<[*const T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html)>

Returns the two raw pointers spanning the slice.

The returned range is half-open, which means that the end pointer
points *one past* the last element of the slice. This way, an empty
slice is represented by two equal pointers, and the difference between
the two pointers represents the size of the slice.

See [ as_ptr](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_ptr) for warnings on using these pointers. The end pointer
requires extra caution, as it does not point to a valid element in the
slice.

This function is useful for interacting with foreign interfaces which use two pointers to refer to a range of elements in memory, as is common in C++.

It can also be useful to check if a pointer to an element refers to an element of this slice:

```
let a = [1, 2, 3];
let x = &a[1] as *const _;
let y = &5 as *const _;
assert!(a.as_ptr_range().contains(&x));
assert!(!a.as_ptr_range().contains(&y));
```

`slice_as_array`)Gets a mutable reference to the slice’s underlying array.

Swaps two elements in the slice.

If `a` equals to `b`, it’s guaranteed that elements won’t change value.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments)Arguments

- a - The index of the first element
- b - The index of the second element

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-4)Panics

Panics if `a` or `b` are out of bounds.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-24)Examples

```
let mut v = ["a", "b", "c", "d", "e"];
v.swap(2, 4);
assert!(v == ["a", "b", "e", "d", "c"]);
```
[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#946)#### pub unsafe fn [swap_unchecked](https://docs.rs#method.swap_unchecked)(&mut self, a: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html), b: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html))

`slice_swap_unchecked`)

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#946)

#### pub unsafe fn [swap_unchecked](https://docs.rs#method.swap_unchecked)(&mut self, a: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html), b: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html))

`slice_swap_unchecked`)Swaps two elements in the slice, without doing bounds checking.

For a safe alternative see [ swap](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.swap).

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments-1)Arguments

- a - The index of the first element
- b - The index of the second element

[§](https://docs.rs#safety-2)Safety

Calling this method with an out-of-bounds index is * undefined behavior*.
The caller has to ensure that

`a < self.len()` and `b < self.len()`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-25)Examples

```
#![feature(slice_swap_unchecked)]
let mut v = ["a", "b", "c", "d"];
// SAFETY: we know that 1 and 3 are both indices of the slice
unsafe { v.swap_unchecked(1, 3) };
assert!(v == ["a", "d", "c", "b"]);
```
Returns an iterator over the slice.

The iterator yields all items from start to end.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-27)Examples

```
let x = &[1, 2, 4];
let mut iterator = x.iter();
assert_eq!(iterator.next(), Some(&1));
assert_eq!(iterator.next(), Some(&2));
assert_eq!(iterator.next(), Some(&4));
assert_eq!(iterator.next(), None);
```
Returns an iterator that allows modifying each value.

The iterator yields all items from start to end.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-28)Examples

```
let x = &mut [1, 2, 4];
for elem in x.iter_mut() {
    *elem += 2;
}
assert_eq!(x, &[3, 4, 6]);
```
Returns an iterator over all contiguous windows of length
`size`. The windows overlap. If the slice is shorter than
`size`, the iterator returns no values.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-5)Panics

Panics if `size` is zero.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-29)Examples

```
let slice = ['l', 'o', 'r', 'e', 'm'];
let mut iter = slice.windows(3);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &['l', 'o', 'r']);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &['o', 'r', 'e']);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &['r', 'e', 'm']);
assert!(iter.next().is_none());
```
If the slice is shorter than `size`:

```
let slice = ['f', 'o', 'o'];
let mut iter = slice.windows(4);
assert!(iter.next().is_none());
```
Because the [Iterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html) trait cannot represent the required lifetimes,
there is no `windows_mut` analog to `windows`;
`[0,1,2].windows_mut(2).collect()` would violate [the rules of references](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch04-02-references-and-borrowing.html#the-rules-of-references)
(though a [LendingIterator](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2022/10/28/gats-stabilization.html) analog is possible). You can sometimes use
[ Cell::as_slice_of_cells](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cell/struct.Cell.html#method.as_slice_of_cells) in
conjunction with

`windows` instead:```
use std::cell::Cell;
let mut array = ['R', 'u', 's', 't', ' ', '2', '0', '1', '5'];
let slice = &mut array[..];
let slice_of_cells: &[Cell<char>] = Cell::from_mut(slice).as_slice_of_cells();
for w in slice_of_cells.windows(3) {
    Cell::swap(&w[0], &w[2]);
}
assert_eq!(array, ['s', 't', ' ', '2', '0', '1', '5', 'u', 'R']);
```
Returns an iterator over `chunk_size` elements of the slice at a time, starting at the
beginning of the slice.

The chunks are slices and do not overlap. If `chunk_size` does not divide the length of the
slice, then the last chunk will not have length `chunk_size`.

See [ chunks_exact](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.chunks_exact) for a variant of this iterator that returns chunks of always exactly

`chunk_size` elements, and [for the same iterator but starting at the end of the slice.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.rchunks)

`rchunks`If your `chunk_size` is a constant, consider using [ as_chunks](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_chunks) instead, which will
give references to arrays of exactly that length, rather than slices.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-6)Panics

Panics if `chunk_size` is zero.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-30)Examples

```
let slice = ['l', 'o', 'r', 'e', 'm'];
let mut iter = slice.chunks(2);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &['l', 'o']);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &['r', 'e']);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &['m']);
assert!(iter.next().is_none());
```

1.31.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1240)#### pub fn [chunks_exact](https://docs.rs#method.chunks_exact)(&self, chunk_size: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)) -> [ChunksExact](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/iter/struct.ChunksExact.html)<'_, T>

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1240)

#### pub fn [chunks_exact](https://docs.rs#method.chunks_exact)(&self, chunk_size: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)) -> [ChunksExact](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/iter/struct.ChunksExact.html)<'_, T>

Returns an iterator over `chunk_size` elements of the slice at a time, starting at the
beginning of the slice.

The chunks are slices and do not overlap. If `chunk_size` does not divide the length of the
slice, then the last up to `chunk_size-1` elements will be omitted and can be retrieved
from the `remainder` function of the iterator.

Due to each chunk having exactly `chunk_size` elements, the compiler can often optimize the
resulting code better than in the case of [ chunks](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.chunks).

See [ chunks](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.chunks) for a variant of this iterator that also returns the remainder as a smaller
chunk, and

[for the same iterator but starting at the end of the slice.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.rchunks_exact)

`rchunks_exact`If your `chunk_size` is a constant, consider using [ as_chunks](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.chunks) instead, which will
give references to arrays of exactly that length, rather than slices.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-8)Panics

Panics if `chunk_size` is zero.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-32)Examples

```
let slice = ['l', 'o', 'r', 'e', 'm'];
let mut iter = slice.chunks_exact(2);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &['l', 'o']);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &['r', 'e']);
assert!(iter.next().is_none());
assert_eq!(iter.remainder(), &['m']);
```

The chunks are mutable slices, and do not overlap. If `chunk_size` does not divide the
length of the slice, then the last up to `chunk_size-1` elements will be omitted and can be

Due to each chunk having exactly `chunk_size` elements, the compiler can often optimize the

smaller chunk, and

`rchunks_exact_mut`If your `chunk_size` is a constant, consider using [ as_chunks_mut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_chunks_mut) instead, which will

let v = &mut [0, 0, 0, 0, 0];

1.88.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1336)#### pub unsafe fn [as_chunks_unchecked](https://docs.rs#method.as_chunks_unchecked)<const N: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(&self) -> &[[[T; N]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.array.html)]

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1336)

#### pub unsafe fn [as_chunks_unchecked](https://docs.rs#method.as_chunks_unchecked)<const N: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(&self) -> &[[[T; N]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.array.html)]

Splits the slice into a slice of `N`-element arrays,
assuming that there’s no remainder.

This is the inverse operation to [ as_flattened](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_flattened).

As this is `unsafe`, consider whether you could use [ as_chunks](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_chunks) or

[instead, perhaps via something like](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_rchunks)

`as_rchunks``if let (chunks, []) = slice.as_chunks()` or
`let (chunks, []) = slice.as_chunks() else { unreachable!() };`.[§](https://docs.rs#safety-3)Safety

This may only be called when

- The slice splits exactly into `N`-element chunks (aka`self.len() % N == 0`).
- `N != 0`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-34)Examples

```
let slice: &[char] = &['l', 'o', 'r', 'e', 'm', '!'];
let chunks: &[[char; 1]] =
    // SAFETY: 1-element chunks never have remainder
    unsafe { slice.as_chunks_unchecked() };
assert_eq!(chunks, &[['l'], ['o'], ['r'], ['e'], ['m'], ['!']]);
let chunks: &[[char; 3]] =
    // SAFETY: The slice length (6) is a multiple of 3
    unsafe { slice.as_chunks_unchecked() };
assert_eq!(chunks, &[['l', 'o', 'r'], ['e', 'm', '!']]);
// These would be unsound:
// let chunks: &[[_; 5]] = slice.as_chunks_unchecked() // The slice length is not a multiple of 5
// let chunks: &[[_; 0]] = slice.as_chunks_unchecked() // Zero-length chunks are never allowed
```
Splits the slice into a slice of `N`-element arrays,
starting at the beginning of the slice,
and a remainder slice with length strictly less than `N`.

The remainder is meaningful in the division sense.  Given
`let (chunks, remainder) = slice.as_chunks()`, then:

- `chunks.len()`equals- `slice.len() / N`,
- `remainder.len()`equals- `slice.len() % N`, and
- `slice.len()`equals- `chunks.len() * N + remainder.len()`.

You can flatten the chunks back into a slice-of-`T` with [ as_flattened](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_flattened).

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-10)Panics

Panics if `N` is zero.

Note that this check is against a const generic parameter, not a runtime value, and thus a particular monomorphization will either always panic or it will never panic.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-35)Examples

```
let slice = ['l', 'o', 'r', 'e', 'm'];
let (chunks, remainder) = slice.as_chunks();
assert_eq!(chunks, &[['l', 'o'], ['r', 'e']]);
assert_eq!(remainder, &['m']);
```
If you expect the slice to be an exact multiple, you can combine
`let`-`else` with an empty slice pattern:

```
let slice = ['R', 'u', 's', 't'];
let (chunks, []) = slice.as_chunks::<2>() else {
    panic!("slice didn't have even length")
};
assert_eq!(chunks, &[['R', 'u'], ['s', 't']]);
```
1.88.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1441)#### pub fn [as_rchunks](https://docs.rs#method.as_rchunks)<const N: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(&self) -> (&[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html), &[[[T; N]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.array.html)])

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1441)

#### pub fn [as_rchunks](https://docs.rs#method.as_rchunks)<const N: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(&self) -> (&[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html), &[[[T; N]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.array.html)])

Splits the slice into a slice of `N`-element arrays,
starting at the end of the slice,
and a remainder slice with length strictly less than `N`.

The remainder is meaningful in the division sense.  Given
`let (remainder, chunks) = slice.as_rchunks()`, then:

- `remainder.len()`equals- `slice.len() % N`,
- `chunks.len()`equals- `slice.len() / N`, and
- `slice.len()`equals- `chunks.len() * N + remainder.len()`.

You can flatten the chunks back into a slice-of-`T` with [ as_flattened](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_flattened).

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-11)Panics

Panics if `N` is zero.

Note that this check is against a const generic parameter, not a runtime value, and thus a particular monomorphization will either always panic or it will never panic.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-36)Examples

```
let slice = ['l', 'o', 'r', 'e', 'm'];
let (remainder, chunks) = slice.as_rchunks();
assert_eq!(remainder, &['l']);
assert_eq!(chunks, &[['o', 'r'], ['e', 'm']]);
```
[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1482)#### pub fn [array_chunks](https://docs.rs#method.array_chunks)<const N: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(&self) -> [ArrayChunks](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/iter/struct.ArrayChunks.html)<'_, T, N>

`array_chunks`)

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1482)

#### pub fn [array_chunks](https://docs.rs#method.array_chunks)<const N: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(&self) -> [ArrayChunks](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/iter/struct.ArrayChunks.html)<'_, T, N>

`array_chunks`)Returns an iterator over `N` elements of the slice at a time, starting at the
beginning of the slice.

The chunks are array references and do not overlap. If `N` does not divide the
length of the slice, then the last up to `N-1` elements will be omitted and can be
retrieved from the `remainder` function of the iterator.

This method is the const generic equivalent of [ chunks_exact](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.chunks_exact).

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-12)Panics

Panics if `N` is zero. This check will most probably get changed to a compile time
error before this method gets stabilized.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-37)Examples

```
#![feature(array_chunks)]
let slice = ['l', 'o', 'r', 'e', 'm'];
let mut iter = slice.array_chunks();
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &['l', 'o']);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &['r', 'e']);
assert!(iter.next().is_none());
assert_eq!(iter.remainder(), &['m']);
```
1.88.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1532)#### pub unsafe fn [as_chunks_unchecked_mut](https://docs.rs#method.as_chunks_unchecked_mut)<const N: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(
    &mut self,
) -> &mut [[[T; N]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.array.html)]

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1532)

#### pub unsafe fn [as_chunks_unchecked_mut](https://docs.rs#method.as_chunks_unchecked_mut)<const N: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(
    &mut self,
) -> &mut [[[T; N]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.array.html)]

Splits the slice into a slice of `N`-element arrays,
assuming that there’s no remainder.

This is the inverse operation to [ as_flattened_mut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_flattened_mut).

As this is `unsafe`, consider whether you could use [ as_chunks_mut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_chunks_mut) or

[instead, perhaps via something like](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_rchunks_mut)

`as_rchunks_mut``if let (chunks, []) = slice.as_chunks_mut()` or
`let (chunks, []) = slice.as_chunks_mut() else { unreachable!() };`.[§](https://docs.rs#safety-4)Safety

This may only be called when

- The slice splits exactly into `N`-element chunks (aka`self.len() % N == 0`).
- `N != 0`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-38)Examples

```
let slice: &mut [char] = &mut ['l', 'o', 'r', 'e', 'm', '!'];
let chunks: &mut [[char; 1]] =
    // SAFETY: 1-element chunks never have remainder
    unsafe { slice.as_chunks_unchecked_mut() };
chunks[0] = ['L'];
assert_eq!(chunks, &[['L'], ['o'], ['r'], ['e'], ['m'], ['!']]);
let chunks: &mut [[char; 3]] =
    // SAFETY: The slice length (6) is a multiple of 3
    unsafe { slice.as_chunks_unchecked_mut() };
chunks[1] = ['a', 'x', '?'];
assert_eq!(slice, &['L', 'o', 'r', 'a', 'x', '?']);
// These would be unsound:
// let chunks: &[[_; 5]] = slice.as_chunks_unchecked_mut() // The slice length is not a multiple of 5
// let chunks: &[[_; 0]] = slice.as_chunks_unchecked_mut() // Zero-length chunks are never allowed
```
1.88.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1586)#### pub fn [as_chunks_mut](https://docs.rs#method.as_chunks_mut)<const N: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(&mut self) -> (&mut [[[T; N]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.array.html)], &mut [[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html))

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1586)

#### pub fn [as_chunks_mut](https://docs.rs#method.as_chunks_mut)<const N: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(&mut self) -> (&mut [[[T; N]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.array.html)], &mut [[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html))

Splits the slice into a slice of `N`-element arrays,
starting at the beginning of the slice,
and a remainder slice with length strictly less than `N`.

The remainder is meaningful in the division sense.  Given
`let (chunks, remainder) = slice.as_chunks_mut()`, then:

- `chunks.len()`equals- `slice.len() / N`,
- `remainder.len()`equals- `slice.len() % N`, and
- `slice.len()`equals- `chunks.len() * N + remainder.len()`.

You can flatten the chunks back into a slice-of-`T` with [ as_flattened_mut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_flattened_mut).

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-13)Panics

Panics if `N` is zero.

Note that this check is against a const generic parameter, not a runtime value, and thus a particular monomorphization will either always panic or it will never panic.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-39)Examples

```
let v = &mut [0, 0, 0, 0, 0];
let mut count = 1;
let (chunks, remainder) = v.as_chunks_mut();
remainder[0] = 9;
for chunk in chunks {
    *chunk = [count; 2];
    count += 1;
}
assert_eq!(v, &[1, 1, 2, 2, 9]);
```

Splits the slice into a slice of `N`-element arrays,
starting at the end of the slice,
and a remainder slice with length strictly less than `N`.

The remainder is meaningful in the division sense.  Given
`let (remainder, chunks) = slice.as_rchunks_mut()`, then:

- `remainder.len()`equals- `slice.len() % N`,
- `chunks.len()`equals- `slice.len() / N`, and
- `slice.len()`equals- `chunks.len() * N + remainder.len()`.

You can flatten the chunks back into a slice-of-`T` with [ as_flattened_mut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_flattened_mut).

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-14)Panics

Panics if `N` is zero.

Note that this check is against a const generic parameter, not a runtime value, and thus a particular monomorphization will either always panic or it will never panic.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-40)Examples

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1682)#### pub fn [array_chunks_mut](https://docs.rs#method.array_chunks_mut)<const N: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(&mut self) -> [ArrayChunksMut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/iter/struct.ArrayChunksMut.html)<'_, T, N>

`array_chunks`)

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1682)

#### pub fn [array_chunks_mut](https://docs.rs#method.array_chunks_mut)<const N: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(&mut self) -> [ArrayChunksMut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/iter/struct.ArrayChunksMut.html)<'_, T, N>

`array_chunks`)Returns an iterator over `N` elements of the slice at a time, starting at the
beginning of the slice.

The chunks are mutable array references and do not overlap. If `N` does not divide
the length of the slice, then the last up to `N-1` elements will be omitted and
can be retrieved from the `into_remainder` function of the iterator.

This method is the const generic equivalent of [ chunks_exact_mut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.chunks_exact_mut).

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-15)Panics

Panics if `N` is zero. This check will most probably get changed to a compile time
error before this method gets stabilized.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-41)Examples

```
#![feature(array_chunks)]
let v = &mut [0, 0, 0, 0, 0];
let mut count = 1;
for chunk in v.array_chunks_mut() {
    *chunk = [count; 2];
    count += 1;
}
assert_eq!(v, &[1, 1, 2, 2, 0]);
```
[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1716)#### pub fn [array_windows](https://docs.rs#method.array_windows)<const N: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(&self) -> [ArrayWindows](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/iter/struct.ArrayWindows.html)<'_, T, N>

`array_windows`)

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1716)

#### pub fn [array_windows](https://docs.rs#method.array_windows)<const N: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(&self) -> [ArrayWindows](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/iter/struct.ArrayWindows.html)<'_, T, N>

`array_windows`)Returns an iterator over overlapping windows of `N` elements of a slice,
starting at the beginning of the slice.

This is the const generic equivalent of [ windows](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.windows).

If `N` is greater than the size of the slice, it will return no windows.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-16)Panics

Panics if `N` is zero. This check will most probably get changed to a compile time
error before this method gets stabilized.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-42)Examples

```
#![feature(array_windows)]
let slice = [0, 1, 2, 3];
let mut iter = slice.array_windows();
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[0, 1]);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[1, 2]);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[2, 3]);
assert!(iter.next().is_none());
```
Returns an iterator over `chunk_size` elements of the slice at a time, starting at the end
of the slice.

The chunks are slices and do not overlap. If `chunk_size` does not divide the length of the
slice, then the last chunk will not have length `chunk_size`.

See [ rchunks_exact](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.rchunks_exact) for a variant of this iterator that returns chunks of always exactly

`chunk_size` elements, and [for the same iterator but starting at the beginning of the slice.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.chunks)

`chunks`If your `chunk_size` is a constant, consider using [ as_rchunks](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_rchunks) instead, which will
give references to arrays of exactly that length, rather than slices.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-17)Panics

Panics if `chunk_size` is zero.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-43)Examples

```
let slice = ['l', 'o', 'r', 'e', 'm'];
let mut iter = slice.rchunks(2);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &['e', 'm']);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &['o', 'r']);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &['l']);
assert!(iter.next().is_none());
```

1.31.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1845)#### pub fn [rchunks_exact](https://docs.rs#method.rchunks_exact)(&self, chunk_size: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)) -> [RChunksExact](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/iter/struct.RChunksExact.html)<'_, T>

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1845)

#### pub fn [rchunks_exact](https://docs.rs#method.rchunks_exact)(&self, chunk_size: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)) -> [RChunksExact](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/iter/struct.RChunksExact.html)<'_, T>

Returns an iterator over `chunk_size` elements of the slice at a time, starting at the
end of the slice.

The chunks are slices and do not overlap. If `chunk_size` does not divide the length of the
slice, then the last up to `chunk_size-1` elements will be omitted and can be retrieved
from the `remainder` function of the iterator.

Due to each chunk having exactly `chunk_size` elements, the compiler can often optimize the
resulting code better than in the case of [ rchunks](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.rchunks).

See [ rchunks](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.rchunks) for a variant of this iterator that also returns the remainder as a smaller
chunk, and

[for the same iterator but starting at the beginning of the slice.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.chunks_exact)

`chunks_exact`If your `chunk_size` is a constant, consider using [ as_rchunks](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_rchunks) instead, which will
give references to arrays of exactly that length, rather than slices.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-19)Panics

Panics if `chunk_size` is zero.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-45)Examples

```
let slice = ['l', 'o', 'r', 'e', 'm'];
let mut iter = slice.rchunks_exact(2);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &['e', 'm']);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &['o', 'r']);
assert!(iter.next().is_none());
assert_eq!(iter.remainder(), &['l']);
```

retrieved from the `into_remainder` function of the iterator.

resulting code better than in the case of [ chunks_mut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.chunks_mut).

See [ rchunks_mut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.rchunks_mut) for a variant of this iterator that also returns the remainder as a
smaller chunk, and

`chunks_exact_mut`If your `chunk_size` is a constant, consider using [ as_rchunks_mut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_rchunks_mut) instead, which will

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-20)Panics

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-46)Examples

```
let v = &mut [0, 0, 0, 0, 0];

for chunk in v.rchunks_exact_mut(2) {
    for elem in chunk.iter_mut() {
        *elem += count;

Returns an iterator over the slice producing non-overlapping runs of elements using the predicate to separate them.

The predicate is called for every pair of consecutive elements,
meaning that it is called on `slice[0]` and `slice[1]`,
followed by `slice[1]` and `slice[2]`, and so on.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-47)Examples

```
let slice = &[1, 1, 1, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2];
let mut iter = slice.chunk_by(|a, b| a == b);
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(&[1, 1, 1][..]));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(&[3, 3][..]));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(&[2, 2, 2][..]));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), None);
```
This method can be used to extract the sorted subslices:

```
let slice = &[1, 1, 2, 3, 2, 3, 2, 3, 4];
let mut iter = slice.chunk_by(|a, b| a <= b);
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(&[1, 1, 2, 3][..]));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(&[2, 3][..]));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(&[2, 3, 4][..]));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), None);
```
1.77.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1976-1978)#### pub fn [chunk_by_mut](https://docs.rs#method.chunk_by_mut)<F>(&mut self, pred: F) -> [ChunkByMut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/iter/struct.ChunkByMut.html)<'_, T, F>

Returns an iterator over the slice producing non-overlapping mutable runs of elements using the predicate to separate them.

The predicate is called for every pair of consecutive elements,
meaning that it is called on `slice[0]` and `slice[1]`,
followed by `slice[1]` and `slice[2]`, and so on.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-48)Examples

assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(&mut [1, 1, 1][..]));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(&mut [3, 3][..]));

This method can be used to extract the sorted subslices:

```

let mut iter = slice.chunk_by_mut(|a, b| a <= b);
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(&mut [1, 1, 2, 3][..]));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(&mut [2, 3][..]));

assert_eq!(iter.next(), None);

Divides one slice into two at an index.

The first will contain all indices from `[0, mid)` (excluding
the index `mid` itself) and the second will contain all
indices from `[mid, len)` (excluding the index `len` itself).

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-21)Panics

Panics if `mid > len`.  For a non-panicking alternative see
[ split_at_checked](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.split_at_checked).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-49)Examples

```
let v = ['a', 'b', 'c'];
{
   let (left, right) = v.split_at(0);
   assert_eq!(left, []);
   assert_eq!(right, ['a', 'b', 'c']);
}
{
    let (left, right) = v.split_at(2);
    assert_eq!(left, ['a', 'b']);
    assert_eq!(right, ['c']);
}
{
    let (left, right) = v.split_at(3);
    assert_eq!(left, ['a', 'b', 'c']);
    assert_eq!(right, []);
}
```

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#2056)

Divides one mutable slice into two at an index.

The first will contain all indices from `[0, mid)` (excluding
the index `mid` itself) and the second will contain all
indices from `[mid, len)` (excluding the index `len` itself).

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-22)Panics

Panics if `mid > len`.  For a non-panicking alternative see
[ split_at_mut_checked](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.split_at_mut_checked).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-50)Examples

```
let mut v = [1, 0, 3, 0, 5, 6];
let (left, right) = v.split_at_mut(2);
assert_eq!(left, [1, 0]);
assert_eq!(right, [3, 0, 5, 6]);
left[1] = 2;
right[1] = 4;
assert_eq!(v, [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]);
```
1.79.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#2108)#### pub unsafe fn [split_at_unchecked](https://docs.rs#method.split_at_unchecked)(&self, mid: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)) -> (&[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html), &[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html))

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#2108)

#### pub unsafe fn [split_at_unchecked](https://docs.rs#method.split_at_unchecked)(&self, mid: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)) -> (&[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html), &[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html))

Divides one slice into two at an index, without doing bounds checking.

The first will contain all indices from `[0, mid)` (excluding
the index `mid` itself) and the second will contain all
indices from `[mid, len)` (excluding the index `len` itself).

For a safe alternative see [ split_at](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.split_at).

[§](https://docs.rs#safety-5)Safety

Calling this method with an out-of-bounds index is * undefined behavior*
even if the resulting reference is not used. The caller has to ensure that

`0 <= mid <= self.len()`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-51)Examples

```
let v = ['a', 'b', 'c'];
unsafe {
   let (left, right) = v.split_at_unchecked(0);
   assert_eq!(left, []);
   assert_eq!(right, ['a', 'b', 'c']);
}
unsafe {
    let (left, right) = v.split_at_unchecked(2);
    assert_eq!(left, ['a', 'b']);
    assert_eq!(right, ['c']);
}
unsafe {
    let (left, right) = v.split_at_unchecked(3);
    assert_eq!(left, ['a', 'b', 'c']);
    assert_eq!(right, []);
}
```
1.79.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#2162)#### pub unsafe fn [split_at_mut_unchecked](https://docs.rs#method.split_at_mut_unchecked)(
    &mut self,
    mid: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
) -> (&mut [[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html), &mut [[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html))

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#2162)

#### pub unsafe fn [split_at_mut_unchecked](https://docs.rs#method.split_at_mut_unchecked)(
    &mut self,
    mid: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
) -> (&mut [[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html), &mut [[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html))

Divides one mutable slice into two at an index, without doing bounds checking.

The first will contain all indices from `[0, mid)` (excluding
the index `mid` itself) and the second will contain all
indices from `[mid, len)` (excluding the index `len` itself).

For a safe alternative see [ split_at_mut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.split_at_mut).

[§](https://docs.rs#safety-6)Safety

Calling this method with an out-of-bounds index is * undefined behavior*
even if the resulting reference is not used. The caller has to ensure that

`0 <= mid <= self.len()`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-52)Examples

```
let mut v = [1, 0, 3, 0, 5, 6];
// scoped to restrict the lifetime of the borrows
unsafe {
    let (left, right) = v.split_at_mut_unchecked(2);
    assert_eq!(left, [1, 0]);
    assert_eq!(right, [3, 0, 5, 6]);
    left[1] = 2;
    right[1] = 4;
}
assert_eq!(v, [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]);
```
Divides one slice into two at an index, returning `None` if the slice is
too short.

If `mid ≤ len` returns a pair of slices where the first will contain all
indices from `[0, mid)` (excluding the index `mid` itself) and the
second will contain all indices from `[mid, len)` (excluding the index
`len` itself).

Otherwise, if `mid > len`, returns `None`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-53)Examples

```
let v = [1, -2, 3, -4, 5, -6];
{
   let (left, right) = v.split_at_checked(0).unwrap();
   assert_eq!(left, []);
   assert_eq!(right, [1, -2, 3, -4, 5, -6]);
}
{
    let (left, right) = v.split_at_checked(2).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(left, [1, -2]);
    assert_eq!(right, [3, -4, 5, -6]);
}
{
    let (left, right) = v.split_at_checked(6).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(left, [1, -2, 3, -4, 5, -6]);
    assert_eq!(right, []);
}
assert_eq!(None, v.split_at_checked(7));
```
1.80.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#2262)#### pub fn [split_at_mut_checked](https://docs.rs#method.split_at_mut_checked)(
    &mut self,
    mid: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<(&mut [[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html), &mut [[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html))>

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#2262)

#### pub fn [split_at_mut_checked](https://docs.rs#method.split_at_mut_checked)(
    &mut self,
    mid: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<(&mut [[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html), &mut [[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html))>

Divides one mutable slice into two at an index, returning `None` if the
slice is too short.

If `mid ≤ len` returns a pair of slices where the first will contain all
indices from `[0, mid)` (excluding the index `mid` itself) and the
second will contain all indices from `[mid, len)` (excluding the index
`len` itself).

Otherwise, if `mid > len`, returns `None`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-54)Examples

```
let mut v = [1, 0, 3, 0, 5, 6];
if let Some((left, right)) = v.split_at_mut_checked(2) {
    assert_eq!(left, [1, 0]);
    assert_eq!(right, [3, 0, 5, 6]);
    left[1] = 2;
    right[1] = 4;
}
assert_eq!(v, [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]);
assert_eq!(None, v.split_at_mut_checked(7));
```
Returns an iterator over subslices separated by elements that match
`pred`. The matched element is not contained in the subslices.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-55)Examples

```
let slice = [10, 40, 33, 20];
let mut iter = slice.split(|num| num % 3 == 0);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[10, 40]);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[20]);
assert!(iter.next().is_none());
```
If the first element is matched, an empty slice will be the first item returned by the iterator. Similarly, if the last element in the slice is matched, an empty slice will be the last item returned by the iterator:

```
let slice = [10, 40, 33];
let mut iter = slice.split(|num| num % 3 == 0);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[10, 40]);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[]);
assert!(iter.next().is_none());
```
If two matched elements are directly adjacent, an empty slice will be present between them:

```
let slice = [10, 6, 33, 20];
let mut iter = slice.split(|num| num % 3 == 0);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[10]);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[]);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[20]);
assert!(iter.next().is_none());
```
Returns an iterator over mutable subslices separated by elements that
match `pred`. The matched element is not contained in the subslices.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-56)Examples

```
let mut v = [10, 40, 30, 20, 60, 50];
for group in v.split_mut(|num| *num % 3 == 0) {
    group[0] = 1;
}
assert_eq!(v, [1, 40, 30, 1, 60, 1]);
```
1.51.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#2372-2374)#### pub fn [split_inclusive](https://docs.rs#method.split_inclusive)<F>(&self, pred: F) -> [SplitInclusive](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/iter/struct.SplitInclusive.html)<'_, T, F>

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#2372-2374)

#### pub fn [split_inclusive](https://docs.rs#method.split_inclusive)<F>(&self, pred: F) -> [SplitInclusive](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/iter/struct.SplitInclusive.html)<'_, T, F>

Returns an iterator over subslices separated by elements that match
`pred`. The matched element is contained in the end of the previous
subslice as a terminator.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-57)Examples

```
let slice = [10, 40, 33, 20];
let mut iter = slice.split_inclusive(|num| num % 3 == 0);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[10, 40, 33]);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[20]);
assert!(iter.next().is_none());
```
If the last element of the slice is matched, that element will be considered the terminator of the preceding slice. That slice will be the last item returned by the iterator.

```
let slice = [3, 10, 40, 33];
let mut iter = slice.split_inclusive(|num| num % 3 == 0);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[3]);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[10, 40, 33]);
assert!(iter.next().is_none());
```
1.51.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#2396-2398)#### pub fn [split_inclusive_mut](https://docs.rs#method.split_inclusive_mut)<F>(&mut self, pred: F) -> [SplitInclusiveMut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/iter/struct.SplitInclusiveMut.html)<'_, T, F>

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#2396-2398)

#### pub fn [split_inclusive_mut](https://docs.rs#method.split_inclusive_mut)<F>(&mut self, pred: F) -> [SplitInclusiveMut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/iter/struct.SplitInclusiveMut.html)<'_, T, F>

Returns an iterator over mutable subslices separated by elements that
match `pred`. The matched element is contained in the previous
subslice as a terminator.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-58)Examples

```
let mut v = [10, 40, 30, 20, 60, 50];
for group in v.split_inclusive_mut(|num| *num % 3 == 0) {
    let terminator_idx = group.len()-1;
    group[terminator_idx] = 1;
}
assert_eq!(v, [10, 40, 1, 20, 1, 1]);
```
Returns an iterator over subslices separated by elements that match
`pred`, starting at the end of the slice and working backwards.
The matched element is not contained in the subslices.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-59)Examples

```
let slice = [11, 22, 33, 0, 44, 55];
let mut iter = slice.rsplit(|num| *num == 0);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[44, 55]);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[11, 22, 33]);
assert_eq!(iter.next(), None);
```
As with `split()`, if the first or last element is matched, an empty
slice will be the first (or last) item returned by the iterator.

```
let v = &[0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8];
let mut it = v.rsplit(|n| *n % 2 == 0);
assert_eq!(it.next().unwrap(), &[]);
assert_eq!(it.next().unwrap(), &[3, 5]);
assert_eq!(it.next().unwrap(), &[1, 1]);
assert_eq!(it.next().unwrap(), &[]);
assert_eq!(it.next(), None);
```
1.27.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#2458-2460)#### pub fn [rsplit_mut](https://docs.rs#method.rsplit_mut)<F>(&mut self, pred: F) -> [RSplitMut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/iter/struct.RSplitMut.html)<'_, T, F>

#### pub fn [rsplit_mut](https://docs.rs#method.rsplit_mut)<F>(&mut self, pred: F) -> [RSplitMut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/iter/struct.RSplitMut.html)<'_, T, F>

Returns an iterator over mutable subslices separated by elements that
match `pred`, starting at the end of the slice and working
backwards. The matched element is not contained in the subslices.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-60)Examples

```
let mut v = [100, 400, 300, 200, 600, 500];
let mut count = 0;
for group in v.rsplit_mut(|num| *num % 3 == 0) {
    count += 1;
    group[0] = count;
}
assert_eq!(v, [3, 400, 300, 2, 600, 1]);
```
Returns an iterator over subslices separated by elements that match
`pred`, limited to returning at most `n` items. The matched element is
not contained in the subslices.

The last element returned, if any, will contain the remainder of the slice.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-61)Examples

Print the slice split once by numbers divisible by 3 (i.e., `[10, 40]`,
`[20, 60, 50]`):

```
let v = [10, 40, 30, 20, 60, 50];
for group in v.splitn(2, |num| *num % 3 == 0) {
    println!("{group:?}");
}
```

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#2595-2597)#### pub fn [split_once](https://docs.rs#method.split_once)<F>(&self, pred: F) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<(&[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html), &[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html))>

`slice_split_once`)

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#2595-2597)

#### pub fn [split_once](https://docs.rs#method.split_once)<F>(&self, pred: F) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<(&[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html), &[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html))>

`slice_split_once`)Splits the slice on the first element that matches the specified predicate.

If any matching elements are present in the slice, returns the prefix
before the match and suffix after. The matching element itself is not
included. If no elements match, returns `None`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-65)Examples

```
#![feature(slice_split_once)]
let s = [1, 2, 3, 2, 4];
assert_eq!(s.split_once(|&x| x == 2), Some((
    &[1][..],
    &[3, 2, 4][..]
)));
assert_eq!(s.split_once(|&x| x == 0), None);
```
[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#2623-2625)#### pub fn [rsplit_once](https://docs.rs#method.rsplit_once)<F>(&self, pred: F) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<(&[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html), &[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html))>

`slice_split_once`)

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#2623-2625)

#### pub fn [rsplit_once](https://docs.rs#method.rsplit_once)<F>(&self, pred: F) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<(&[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html), &[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html))>

`slice_split_once`)Splits the slice on the last element that matches the specified predicate.

If any matching elements are present in the slice, returns the prefix
before the match and suffix after. The matching element itself is not
included. If no elements match, returns `None`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-66)Examples

```
#![feature(slice_split_once)]
let s = [1, 2, 3, 2, 4];
assert_eq!(s.rsplit_once(|&x| x == 2), Some((
    &[1, 2, 3][..],
    &[4][..]
)));
assert_eq!(s.rsplit_once(|&x| x == 0), None);
```
Returns `true` if the slice contains an element with the given value.

This operation is *O*(*n*).

Note that if you have a sorted slice, [ binary_search](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.binary_search) may be faster.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-67)Examples

```
let v = [10, 40, 30];
assert!(v.contains(&30));
assert!(!v.contains(&50));
```
If you do not have a `&T`, but some other value that you can compare
with one (for example, `String` implements `PartialEq<str>`), you can
use `iter().any`:

```
let v = [String::from("hello"), String::from("world")]; // slice of `String`
assert!(v.iter().any(|e| e == "hello")); // search with `&str`
assert!(!v.iter().any(|e| e == "hi"));
```
1.0.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#2689-2691)#### pub fn [starts_with](https://docs.rs#method.starts_with)(&self, needle: &[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#2689-2691)

#### pub fn [starts_with](https://docs.rs#method.starts_with)(&self, needle: &[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Returns `true` if `needle` is a prefix of the slice or equal to the slice.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-68)Examples

```
let v = [10, 40, 30];
assert!(v.starts_with(&[10]));
assert!(v.starts_with(&[10, 40]));
assert!(v.starts_with(&v));
assert!(!v.starts_with(&[50]));
assert!(!v.starts_with(&[10, 50]));
```
Always returns `true` if `needle` is an empty slice:

```
let v = &[10, 40, 30];
assert!(v.starts_with(&[]));
let v: &[u8] = &[];
assert!(v.starts_with(&[]));
```
Returns `true` if `needle` is a suffix of the slice or equal to the slice.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-69)Examples

```
let v = [10, 40, 30];
assert!(v.ends_with(&[30]));
assert!(v.ends_with(&[40, 30]));
assert!(v.ends_with(&v));
assert!(!v.ends_with(&[50]));
assert!(!v.ends_with(&[50, 30]));
```
Always returns `true` if `needle` is an empty slice:

```
let v = &[10, 40, 30];
assert!(v.ends_with(&[]));
let v: &[u8] = &[];
assert!(v.ends_with(&[]));
```
1.51.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#2752-2754)#### pub fn [strip_prefix](https://docs.rs#method.strip_prefix)<P>(&self, prefix: [&P](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html)>

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#2752-2754)

#### pub fn [strip_prefix](https://docs.rs#method.strip_prefix)<P>(&self, prefix: [&P](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html)>

Returns a subslice with the prefix removed.

If the slice starts with `prefix`, returns the subslice after the prefix, wrapped in `Some`.
If `prefix` is empty, simply returns the original slice. If `prefix` is equal to the
original slice, returns an empty slice.

If the slice does not start with `prefix`, returns `None`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-70)Examples

```
let v = &[10, 40, 30];
assert_eq!(v.strip_prefix(&[10]), Some(&[40, 30][..]));
assert_eq!(v.strip_prefix(&[10, 40]), Some(&[30][..]));
assert_eq!(v.strip_prefix(&[10, 40, 30]), Some(&[][..]));
assert_eq!(v.strip_prefix(&[50]), None);
assert_eq!(v.strip_prefix(&[10, 50]), None);
let prefix : &str = "he";
assert_eq!(b"hello".strip_prefix(prefix.as_bytes()),
           Some(b"llo".as_ref()));
```
1.51.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#2788-2790)#### pub fn [strip_suffix](https://docs.rs#method.strip_suffix)<P>(&self, suffix: [&P](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html)>

#### pub fn [strip_suffix](https://docs.rs#method.strip_suffix)<P>(&self, suffix: [&P](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html)>

Returns a subslice with the suffix removed.

If the slice ends with `suffix`, returns the subslice before the suffix, wrapped in `Some`.
If `suffix` is empty, simply returns the original slice. If `suffix` is equal to the
original slice, returns an empty slice.

If the slice does not end with `suffix`, returns `None`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-71)Examples

```
let v = &[10, 40, 30];
assert_eq!(v.strip_suffix(&[30]), Some(&[10, 40][..]));
assert_eq!(v.strip_suffix(&[40, 30]), Some(&[10][..]));
assert_eq!(v.strip_suffix(&[10, 40, 30]), Some(&[][..]));
assert_eq!(v.strip_suffix(&[50]), None);
assert_eq!(v.strip_suffix(&[50, 30]), None);
```
